alignments.note: Participle rendered as a finite subordinate clause; the supplied subordinator 'when' and the copula 'were' are helpers on it under rules 7, 9 and 31.

The article fills the determiner slot as the supplied possessive 'our', and carries the dative preposition 'through' with it under rule 21; alternatively 'through' could sit with the noun and 'our' alone realize the article.
Resultative rendering heads on the meaning-bearing complement 'alive' (rule 17); supplied object 'us' is a helper, and 'together' realizes the συν- prefix while 'with' stays with the dative noun.
Article before a name with no English realization (rule 23).
The article being unrepresented, the case preposition 'with' stays with the noun (rule 20).
'by' realizes the dative case; the noun is the head (rule 17).

Periphrastic perfect: the finite εἰμί supplies subject 'ye' and the auxiliary chain 'have ... been', headed on the copula 'been'; the perfect marker 'have' could defensibly attach to the participle instead.
